physical_intent: Show oil poured into water, remaining separate and settling as a layer above the water.

scene.environment: Transparent receiving glass on a table.
process_objects: separate oil droplets or patches at the water surface

semantic_keyframes.visible_state: Water is already in the receiving glass; oil remains in the source container.
semantic_keyframes.physical_state: The liquids are separate and have not contacted each other.
must_not_show: oil already inside the receiving glass

semantic_keyframes.visible_state: Oil leaves the source container and begins falling toward the water surface.
semantic_keyframes.physical_state: Gravity transfers oil from the source toward the receiving glass.

semantic_keyframes.visible_state: Oil has contacted the water and remains distinct as small droplets or patches near the surface.
semantic_keyframes.physical_state: Oil and water are immiscible; the oil separates instead of dissolving.
must_not_show: deep sinking oil as the dominant behavior

semantic_keyframes.visible_state: Separate oil patches spread and coalesce across the water surface.
semantic_keyframes.physical_state: Accumulated oil spreads laterally near the surface and starts forming a continuous layer.
must_not_show: oil patches disappearing before the layer grows

semantic_keyframes.visible_state: A stable oil layer sits above the water with a visible boundary.
semantic_keyframes.physical_state: The immiscible liquids settle into stratified layers.
must_not_show: oil below water as the final arrangement

transitions.cause: The source container is tilted and gravity pulls oil out.
transitions.continuous_change: The change originates at the source lip; oil moves downward along a visible transfer path toward the receiving glass, so material in the receiving glass is connected to oil leaving the source.
should_not_jump: oil appears in the receiving glass without a transfer path
surface oil patches appear before falling oil reaches the water

transitions.cause: Falling oil contacts the water surface.
transitions.continuous_change: The change originates at the water contact point; falling oil accumulates there as distinct droplets or small patches near the surface instead of appearing elsewhere.
should_not_jump: a full surface layer appears immediately at contact

transitions.cause: Immiscible oil accumulates at the surface and spreads laterally.
transitions.continuous_change: Small droplets or patches spread outward from the contact region, widen laterally, and merge while visible oil coverage increases smoothly.
should_not_jump: patches shrink away before a new layer appears
a sudden geometric disk replaces the patches

transitions.cause: Coalesced oil settles into a stable layer above the denser water.
transitions.continuous_change: Patchy surface coverage becomes a smoother continuous top layer while preserving the same surface footprint and sharpening the oil-water boundary.
should_not_jump: final layer appears as an unrelated new object

causal_constraints.after: oil appears in the receiving glass
causal_constraints.reason: Transferred material must come from the source.

causal_constraints.after: oil patches spread across the surface
causal_constraints.reason: Surface spreading requires contact and accumulation.
The final layer should be the result of accumulated oil, not an immediate geometric disk.

must_show: oil and water remain visually distinct
oil patches spread before final layer
must_avoid: oil dissolves uniformly into the water
oil sinks permanently to the bottom
sudden circular or geometric oil film appears without buildup
uncertain_assumptions: Assume the oil is less dense than water unless the input says otherwise.
